title: Bosun PKM Postel Coercion Contract v1
description: Reusable Draft 2020-12 $defs for Postel's Principle: be liberal in what you accept, conservative in what you emit. JSON Schema cannot perform coercion — it only validates accepted (liberal) input shapes. Runtime ingest MUST coerce a scalar canonical URN to a one-element array and a date-only string to midnight UTC (`T00:00:00Z`). Emitters MUST write arrays of URNs and full UTC date-times ending in Z. The root object is an acid-test envelope over those $defs, not a note contract.

date_only.description: Date-only example (`YYYY-MM-DD`); acceptors default this to 00:00:00Z.

datetime_utc.description: Conservative emit example: full ISO-8601 UTC date-time ending in Z.

scalar_urn.description: Scalar URN example; acceptors coerce this to a one-element array.

urn_array.description: Conservative emit example: non-empty unique array of canonical URNs.

canonicalUrn.description: Canonical URN `urn:<realm>:<entity_type>:<uuid>`. Realm-specific predicates in relations.schema.json tighten the realm and entity_type.

urnOrUrnArray.description: Liberal accept shape for one-or-more canonical URNs. A single matching string or a non-empty unique array of matching strings both validate. JSON Schema does not coerce; emitters MUST write an array even for one target.

dateOnly.description: Date-only input (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Acceptors MUST default the time to 00:00:00Z.

utcDateTime.description: Full ISO-8601 UTC date-time ending in Z. `format: date-time` is the RFC 3339 annotation for format-aware validators; the Z pattern is the portable constraint. Emitters MUST write this shape.

dateOrDateTime.description: Liberal accept shape for timestamps. Date-only strings and full UTC date-times both validate. JSON Schema does not coerce; emitters MUST write full UTC date-times.
